packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-14 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (working notes appended image by image; summary at end)

== image-001.jpg (overview, reduced) ==
Object: parchment strips used as spine lining of a bound book, seen looking down the open spine from the
tail (endband and text-block edge at the bottom of the photo, a transparent mm/cm scale at right reading 0-9).
Thread-wrapped double sewing supports on brown (tawed/tanned) leather thongs divide the lining into panels.
At least three written panels are visible, plus a small piece at the very top right:
 - lower panel (scale c. 0-1.5 cm): script appears UPSIDE DOWN relative to the camera;
 - middle panel (scale c. 2-5 cm): script UPRIGHT, 7 lines, the clearest;
 - upper panel (scale c. 5.5-8.5 cm): script UPSIDE DOWN again;
 - topmost scrap (c. 9 cm): a few red-brown letters.
Script: a rounded, fairly large gothic bookhand with cursive features (two-compartment a, looped d, 2-shaped r,
long s), in a pale orange-brown ink; a few words in a much darker black-brown ink (last line of the middle panel,
some marginal letters). Many abbreviation strokes. Ruling in plummet/lead: horizontal lines for every text
line and vertical bounding lines; a wide ruled but empty band lies to the left of the text block in the middle
panel (tentative: an outer margin or intercolumnar space with marginal notes at its far left edge).
No rubric, running title or coloured initial visible. Modern typed purple letters ("fa", "he") and pencil/ink
notes on the paper at right belong to the modern volume, not the fragment.

== image-002.jpg (native tile: middle panel and lower panel) ==
MIDDLE PANEL, main text block (line beginnings at the vertical ruling; right ends cut by the lining edge):
 image-002 L1: m ſ?ip?' ex ꝑ? tlis[..]        (top line, partly under the sewing; "ex" clear; before it "ſiꝑ"/"gip'"; after it a p-form with stroke, then "tlis" / "ctis" with a stroke)
 image-002 L2: g'? aɔcn̄i? ꝑ lr̄ā it[..]        (first sign an 8-like "g"/"s" with superscript hook: "ſ(ed)"? / "g(ra)"? ; then a word of a + two c/t-like letters + minims with stroke above: "accn̄i"/"attm̄"; then "ꝑ" (per), "lr̄ā" = l(itte)rā(m)?, "it"/"ic" cut)
 image-002 L3: ens nō tm̄ litat?[..]           ("ens" or "cns"; "nō" = no(n); "tm̄"/"tn̄" = t(antu)m / t(ame)n; "litat"/"litar" with a mark above the t, cut)
 image-002 L4: iſtū? motum inte[..]           (first word: long-s ligature + "tū" with stroke: "iſtu(m)" / "illū"; "motum" clear, written "motū" + minims; "inte"/"intc" cut)
 image-002 L5: ut ē motus ad v?[..]           ("ut" or "vt"; "ē" = e(st); "motus" (2-shaped final s / "moꝛus"?); "ad"; then a letter cut by the edge)
 image-002 L6: ñle . ſ? . p? tectoie? a[..]   (THIS LINE IN DARK INK. "ñle" with stroke = n(atur)ale? / n(u)lle?; then a point, a small letter (s/c), a point, "p" or "ꝑ"; then a word "tectoie"/"rectōe"/"ꝓtectōe" with stroke above the end; then "a"/"ac" cut. A blue-green line runs under the end of this line.)
MIDDLE PANEL, far-left edge (ends of lines of another column, or marginal notes; only last letters visible), top to bottom:
 image-002 M1: [..]o
 image-002 M2: [..]no .   (dark ink)
 image-002 M3: [..]e     (dark ink)
 image-002 M4: [..]c?le . / [..]ele
 image-002 M5: [..]at? / [..]ar
 image-002 M6: [..]7? (a mark like tironian et or a paragraph hook)
LOWER PANEL (script inverted in this view; I have not rotated the image, so readings here are provisional and
taken by reading the letters upside down; see later tiles):
 two blocks separated by a vertical ruling and an empty band; right block (camera view) shows about 4 lines,
 left block about 5 lines; one darker word at bottom left ("[..]u" after minims). To be read from tiles.

== image-003.jpg (second overview, reduced: same spine photographed from the opposite end) ==
Camera is turned 180 degrees relative to image-001 (scale now at left reading 0-9 downward, endband at top).
In this view the panel nearest the endband (0-1.5 cm) and the panel at 5.5-8 cm are UPRIGHT and the middle
panel (2-4.5 cm) is INVERTED. So the strips were pasted in alternating orientation: the middle strip is turned
180 degrees relative to its neighbours. (Observation. Tentative interpretation: strips cut from the same or
similar leaves and laid in head-to-tail.) Each strip shows two text blocks separated by a ruled empty band,
i.e. either two columns with their intercolumnar space, or text plus a wide margin carrying notes.
First pass from this overview:
 panel at 0-1.5 cm, left block (line ends):   "[..]i oꝛue?" / "[..]e m-itez ." / "[..]no  ...att" / "[..]o ſ[..]"
 panel at 0-1.5 cm, right block (line starts): "in mā[..]" (dark ink) / "eia? ma[..]" / "tc ite? i[..]" / "[..]e[..]"
 panel at 5.5-8 cm: see image-004.

== image-004.jpg (native tile: the 5.5-8 cm panel, upright in this view, photographed obliquely) ==
LEFT BLOCK (line ends? the strip is cut at its left by the lining edge; a vertical ruling follows on the right,
so these are the right-hand ends of lines of one block), top to bottom:
 image-004 L1: [..]ꝺ?ictas? / [..]uitas            (orange ink; "-tas" clear)
 image-004 L2: ꝛ̊? e? [..] cog?ſa? / [..]aſſa        (a sign with superscript at the start; a word ending "-gſa"/"-ſſa" with final flourish)
 image-004 L3: [..]m cog?ſ[..]  ... ı̄t?iligēt? / ꝯtingēt   (two words; the second in DARK ink with stroke over the end: "ītelligēt" (intelligent-/-ur?) or "ꝯtingēt"; small dark superscript marks above it)
 image-004 L4: [dark smudged word] [..]                  ("it?m̄"? - dark ink, blurred)
 image-004 L5: [.]eꝺis? p̄o? :                           (orange "eꝺis"/"eclis"/"tedis" then DARK "po" with superscript o / stroke = p(ri)o? / p(rim)o?, then two points)
 image-004 L6: ꝺ' : tn̄? ħ?tet? / hr̄et                   (dark ink: a d-form with hook (ꝺ(icitu)r?/ꝺ(e)?), points, then "tñ"/"ñ", then a word "hr̄et"/"htet" = h(abe)ret? )
RIGHT BLOCK (line beginnings at the vertical ruling; strongly foreshortened and partly out of focus):
 image-004 R1: [..]alis? m[..]   / "nulis"
 image-004 R2: [..]mlis? in[..]
 image-004 R3: mim?[..] (minims) ... t?ꝑt?[..]
 image-004 R4: ſ?ꝑ? [.] tꝑꝛ?[..] / "ſup t tpꝛ"
 image-004 R5: ens . n [..]c[..] / "cns . n"
 image-004 R6: ꝺ?ꝛca? fi?ꝛ?[..] / "ꝺicta ſic[..]"
 These right-block readings are weak; a frontal native tile is needed (see later images).
TOP OF TILE (the inverted middle panel, bottom lines seen upside down): corresponds to image-002 L1-L2.
BOTTOM OF TILE (9 cm scrap, out of focus): "[..]i ħ?[..]" - two or three orange letters, not legible.

== image-005.jpg and image-006.jpg (two crops of the same oblique close view; 006 is the tighter crop of 005 - OVERLAP, same five lines) ==
A different viewing angle (looking along the spine, strong raking/oblique view, somewhat overexposed). One panel
between two leather-thong supports; text UPRIGHT; five ruled lines; the left part of every line disappears into
the fold. Whether this panel is one of those in image-001/003 or a further one I cannot tell from the crop
(its wording does not repeat the middle panel of image-002).
 image-006 L1: [..]e? mħ?utas? v?[..]       (a word with an h-like ascender and stroke, ending "-tas": "mħitas"/"nihilitas"?/"-uitas"; then a v/b-like letter cut at right)
 image-006 L2: [..]ul? . pħs? tn̄ q[..]       ("pħs" with stroke through the ascender = ph(ilosoph)us? or "pl'is" = pl(ur)is?; "tn̄"/"tm̄" = t(ame)n / t(antu)m; "q" cut)
 image-006 L3: [..]ꝯ? hōi eē ñle .           ("hōi" = ho(min)i; "eē" = e(ss)e; "ñle" in DARK ink with stroke = n(atur)ale?; final point)
 image-006 L4: [..]ꝛat . n' v̄te? cogn[..]    ("n'" with superscript = n(isi)?/n(e)c?; "v̄te"/"vōe" with stroke = v(er)i(ta)te? / v(ir)t(ut)e?; "cogn-"/"cogit-" cut)
 image-006 L5: [..]a foꝛtt? ꝺꝛ? m?[..]       ("foꝛtt"/"foꝛtu" - forti-/fortu-; then "ꝺꝛ" (= d(icitu)r?) and a dark-ink descender/letter "m"/"in" below-right)
 (image-005 L1-L5 are the same lines; in 005 the supports above and below are also visible, no extra text.)

== image-007.jpg (oblique close view of another panel; text INVERTED in this view) ==
Layout: vertical ruling with an empty ruled band to its left (in camera view) and, further left, blurred ends of
another block; to the right, line-beginnings/ends of a block, 6 lines, the 3rd-5th partly in dark ink and abraded.
Above the upper support, part of the next panel (also inverted) with 3-4 lines out of focus.
Read by turning the letters mentally (provisional; see the note on rotation in the summary):
 image-007 (top line in camera view = last line of the strip):   "[..] ꝯ? cen? ɔ" - orange, large: seen inverted as "6 ɔǝɔ"; provisional "ꝺ ...ccꝺ"
 image-007 (bottom line in camera view = first line of the strip): a word of c. 6 letters, orange, provisional "eccꝺa"/"ecclia"-like shapes - NOT secure
 dark-ink words in between: "a ch"? and "q m"? (seen inverted as "ɥɔ ɐ" / "ɯ b")
 I treat this tile as unread pending a rotated look.

NOTE ON ROTATION: because several strips are inverted in the photographs, I made 180-degree rotated copies /
crops of image-002, image-004 and image-008 in a scratch folder of my own (derived only from the packet images)
and read from those. Line numbers below still refer to the ORIGINAL image; for inverted panels I count lines in
text order (first text line = lowest in the original image) and say so.

== image-008.jpg (tighter crop of image-007 - OVERLAP; panel inverted in the photo; read from a rotated copy) ==
Layout after rotation: text block at LEFT (only the last 1-2 words of each line survive, left part cut by the
lining edge), then a vertical ruling, a ruled EMPTY band, then at far right the blurred beginnings of another
block (not legible). Small "=" marks stand after lines 3 and 4 just outside the ruling (line-fillers or
hyphen/continuation strokes). Text order (line 1 = bottom of original image-008):
 image-008 T1: [..]t? eccq?a .        (orange; letters t/r + e + c + c + q-or-ꝺ + a + point; "aliqua"/"eccl(esi)a"-like shapes, not resolved)
 image-008 T2: [..]o q̄ m̄? .           ("o" orange; then DARK ink "q̄" with stroke (= q(ue)/q(uam)?) and "m"/"in" with a mark, point)
 image-008 T3: [..]e ag? ele =        ("e a"+g-like letter orange; "ele"/"cle" in DARK ink; "=" after)
 image-008 T4: [..] [dark, abraded: "ꝑ?ſt?ꝰ"? ... "eiꝰ"?] =    (surface rubbed; not legible)
 image-008 T5: [..]x?ceꝺit            (orange; "exceꝺit" or "acceꝺit"; -ceꝺit clear)
 image-008 T6: [..]is? cet?[..]       (orange; "vō"/"is" then "cet-"/"cer-", cut by the support)

== image-002.jpg LOWER PANEL (nearest the endband), read from a rotated copy; text order (line 1 = lowest in original image-002) ==
Layout after rotation: left block = line ENDS; vertical ruling; ruled EMPTY band (pierced by the endband
tie-downs); vertical ruling; right block = line BEGINNINGS.
 left block:
 image-002 low-L1: [..]a? oꝛ uo?[..]     ("oꝛ" with 2-shaped r; then "uo"/"ue" damaged at the tie-down)
 image-002 low-L2: [..]c? nā? īteꝰ? .     (a word "na"/"nā", then "īteꝰ"/"iteꝛ" with stroke and final -us/-er hook, point: possibly int(er)/it(er)- )
 image-002 low-L3: [..]m / [..]o ꝑ?oꝛt?[..]  (small "m" written above the line level, then "o", then a word with p + "oꝛt"/"att" and a final flourish)
 image-002 low-L4: [..]ſo? ſ?cꝛ?[..]      (cut by the support: "ſo ſeꝛ.."/"io ſcri.." )
 right block:
 image-002 low-R1: in mi?ll?[..]          (DARK ink; "in" then minims and tall letters, top cut by the endband: "in mill-"/"in null-"/"in multi-")
 image-002 low-R2: cāa? w?ō? i' on[..]    ("cāa"/"eāa" with stroke (c(aus)a?); a blurred word; then "i" with hook and "on"/"ou" at the edge)
 image-002 low-R3: tc? ēte? [..]ꝺ?[..]    ("tc"/"tt"; "ēte"/"īte" with stroke; rest under the curve of the strip)
 image-002 low-R4: [..] e ꝑ?t?[..]        (traces above the support)

== image-009.jpg and image-010.jpg (two crops of one oblique view; 010 tighter - OVERLAP) ==
The endband panel again (tie-down threads at upper left), upright, seen very obliquely from the side; the
right-hand part of the strip is lifted/bent toward the camera, so the right block's continuation is visible here
that was hidden in image-002:
 image-010 L1: [..] . tt? / ꝛ.tt        (dark dot/letter then orange "tt"/"cc" - at the tie-down)
 image-010 L2: [..]mā? [..]  tt? ēe      (left: dark "ma"/"mā" (= image-002 low-R1); right on the bent part: "tt"/"tc" then "ēe" with stroke = e(ss)e, the last letter in dark ink)
 image-010 L3: [..]ia? vacc?t [..] ꝺ?unh? / ꝺanh   (left "cāa vacc.."/"-ia wō.." (= low-R2); right: a word beginning with a looped d: "ꝺunh"/"ꝺanb"/"ꝺault")
 image-010 L4: tc ite ꝺ[..]  ... eo? .   (left "tc īte ꝺ" (= low-R3); right: "eo ."/"co ." )
 image-010 L5: [..]l' ꝑt?[..]            (traces)
 Below the support (bottom of 009): the next panel, inverted, same words as image-007/008 top ("[..]is cet", "[..]ceꝺit").
 => so the panel of image-007/008 is the one adjacent to the endband panel, i.e. the "middle panel" of
 image-001 seen from its other (left-margin) side? NO: its wording (exceꝺit, q̄ m̄, ele) does not match the
 middle panel's main block; it matches the middle panel's FAR-LEFT edge letters (image-002 M2 "no .", M3 "e",
 M4 "cle"/"ele") only loosely. I leave the correspondence open.

== image-011.jpg and image-012.jpg (two crops of one view; 012 tighter - OVERLAP) ==
A very oblique, blurred look into the narrowing gap at a fourth strip (with a blob of adhesive and a white
slip/flag in the foreground). About 6 lines, orange with some dark-ink words; ruling visible.
 image-012 L1: [.]' fu?it? [..]k?[..]    (orange: a letter with hook, then a word like "fuit"/"ſint"/"hnt"; beyond the ruling dark traces)
 image-012 L2: [..] [dark] ꝑ?[..]          (dark-ink sign resembling "ꝑ"/"ꝓ" or a paragraph mark, with strokes)
 image-012 L3: [..]t? [..]
 image-012 L4: [..] ē? i?a? [..]           ("ē" with stroke; minims)
 image-012 L5: [..]i?i? [..]
 image-012 L6: [dark traces]
 Effectively unread: out of focus and foreshortened. A frontal native tile of this fourth strip is needed.

== image-013.jpg (third overview, reduced: the spine opened from the other joint, endband at top, a finger at bottom) ==
Shows the OTHER ends of the same transverse strips where they emerge on the far side of the sewing supports -
four narrow written tabs in a vertical row between the leather thong ends:
 tab 1 (nearest endband, upright):  "[..]t ꝺ" / "tc ēe" / "[..]nh"-like word / "eo ."      = image-009/010
 tab 2 (inverted):                  "[..]is cet" / "[..]ceꝺit" / [abraded dark] / "e ag ele" / "q̄ m̄" / "eccqa"   = image-007/008
 tab 3 (upright):                   "[..]tas v" / "tn̄ q" / "ñle ." / "cogn" / "ꝺꝛm"          = image-005/006
 tab 4 (orientation unclear, partly hidden): "ꝑ"/"p"-like dark sign, a few orange letters      = image-011/012
Orientation alternates tab to tab, as in image-001/003. Tentative physical correlation (observation-based, not
certain): tab 1 = the endband panel of image-001/003; tab 2 = the far-left edge of the middle panel (compare
image-002 M2 dark "no ." with image-008 T2 dark "q̄ m̄ ."/"q̄ no .", M3 dark "e" with T3 dark "ele", M4 "cle ."
with T4); tab 3 = the 5.5-8 cm panel (compare image-004 L1 "-tas" with image-006 L1 "-tas v"), though the line
counts do not align cleanly and I do not merge the readings.

== image-014.jpg, image-015.jpg, image-016.jpg (native tiles running down image-013; they overlap one another and repeat tabs 1-4) ==
image-014 (tab 1, upright; then top of tab 2):
 image-014 L1: [..]c?t ꝺ[..]        (dark-ink "ct"/"tt" at the tie-down, then orange looped "ꝺ" cut at right)
 image-014 L2: tc eē                ("tc"/"tt" orange; "eē" with stroke = e(ss)e, second e in dark ink)
 image-014 L3: [.]anh?b?[..]        (a word with two ascenders: "ꝺanh.."/"[.]unhi.."/"ambi.."; a corner of the tab is folded over its end)
 image-014 L4: eo? .                ("eo"/"co" dark-edged, point; on the folded corner faint offset letters)
 image-014 L5-6 (tab 2, INVERTED; as seen): = image-008 T6 "[..]is cet", T5 "[..]ceꝺit" (overlap)
image-015 (tab 2 inverted, then top of tab 3 upright):
 tab 2, in text order (bottom of the tab first): 
   T1 "[..]eccq?a" (orange; here the letters look like e-c-c-q/ꝺ-a with the first letter t/r lost)
   T2 "[..] q̄ [.]i?" (DARK "q" with a bar under/over it, and a dark minim letter beside)
   T3 "[..]e ag? [.]e[.]" (orange "ag"/"aꝺ", dark "e", dark stroke)
   T4 [dark, abraded; "ꝑ?ſt?" and a 7-shaped sign]
